Figure 9:  Four latent action learning paradigms.
An encoder maps a visual transition to a variational latent  z t z_{t} .
The prediction targets are (a) the observed action  a t a_{t} , (b) the future image  x t + 1 x_{t+1} ,
(c) frozen DINOv3 features  f t + 1 f_{t+1} , and (d) both the image and action.
Reconstruction decoders additionally receive the current image or its features.
In (d), pixel reconstruction uses all samples, while the action loss uses only labeled samples.
All variants include the same form of KL regularization.

Figure 10:  Visualization of the semantic separability of latent actions learned by four LAM paradigms across different navigation action categories. TartanDrive and Go Stanford are out-of-domain datasets.
